Study objective

This report evaluates associations and prediction of the heart disease label using generalized linear models. It is an educational exercise, not a validated medical diagnostic system.

The original collaborative notebooks are preserved in the team source repository. This report uses a cleaned, self-contained analysis pipeline.

Data quality and evaluation design

original_rows unique_rows exact_duplicates_removed train_rows test_rows original_prevalence deduplicated_prevalence test_prevalence
1025 302 723 241 61 0.513 0.543 0.541

The raw heart dataset contains many exact duplicate rows. We removed duplicates before stratified training/testing division and selected model parameters only from training data. This prevents identical data rows from being shared between the training and held-out test partitions.

Models and held-out evaluation

We compared full logistic regression, stepwise logistic regression (AIC selection on training data), and L1-penalized logistic regression (LASSO, lambda selected by five-fold cross-validation within training data). Categorical coded predictors were treated as factors and the test set was never used to choose predictors or the regularization parameter.

Limitations

  • The dataset is a small, duplicated, historical Cleveland-derived sample.
  • The reported scores are from one deterministic held-out split rather than repeated external validation. They are not an estimate of prospective clinical performance with reliable uncertainty bounds.
  • This is association and prediction, not causal inference.
  • Disease-label definitions and source coding require caution.
  • Do not use these models to make health or treatment decisions.
